This year, gas prices jumped almost sixty percent in just four months.

America has been here before.

October 1973: Arab oil producers cut off oil to the United States.

Crude went from about three dollars a barrel to nearly twelve. Gas rose from thirty-nine cents to fifty-three.

Doesn't sound like much? Price controls kept the pump price down, but supplies ran short, and drivers waited hours in line. Congress even set a national speed limit: fifty-five miles an hour.

Then 1979 brought a second shock. By 1981, gas cost three and a half times its 1973 price.

Adjusted for inflation, that's still higher than today.

The big difference in 2026? No price controls, and no lines. Just the bill. The American File.
